questions.stem: Which of the following is a property of non-metals?
choices: They are good conductors of electricity
They are malleable and ductile
They form positive ions by losing electrons
They form oxides which are either acidic or neutral
questions.solution: Non-metals form oxides that are either acidic or neutral, which is a characteristic property of non-metals. Metals, in contrast, are good conductors of electricity and are malleable and ductile, which are not traits of non-metals. Non-metals tend to gain electrons, forming negative ions, not positive ions as suggested in one of the options.

questions.stem: If a metal 'X' produces a colourless gas when reacted with dilute sulphuric acid, and the gas burns with a 'pop' sound, which of the following could 'X' be?
choices: Copper
Iron
Zinc
Sodium
questions.solution: Sodium reacts vigorously with dilute sulphuric acid to produce hydrogen gas, which burns with a 'pop' sound. Copper does not react with dilute sulphuric acid. Iron and zinc produce hydrogen but not as vigorously as sodium. Sodium is the most reactive among the options and would produce the described gas.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about the chemical properties of non-metals?
choices: They form basic oxides when dissolved in water
They are good conductors of electricity
They are generally soft and malleable
They produce acidic oxides when dissolved in water
questions.solution: Non-metals typically produce acidic oxides when dissolved in water, which is a general chemical property of non-metals. Metals, in contrast, form basic oxides, and non-metals are poor conductors of electricity, making the other options incorrect. Non-metals are also generally brittle, not soft and malleable.
